facts.statement: Kansas requires a driving speed that is reasonable for the conditions present.
Choose speed after considering road conditions, weather, the vehicle and your physical condition.
The listed normal-condition maximums do not remove the need to reduce speed for special hazards.
Unless a different limit is posted, an urban district has a maximum speed of 30 miles per hour.
Outside towns, the maximum is 75 miles per hour on a separated multilane highway designated and posted by the Secretary of Transportation, unless a different limit is posted.
Outside towns, a state or federal highway has a maximum speed of 65 miles per hour unless a different limit is posted.
Outside towns, a county or township road has a maximum speed of 55 miles per hour unless a different limit is posted.
A properly marked school zone has a 20-mile-per-hour maximum unless posted otherwise.
A properly marked business district has a 20-mile-per-hour maximum unless posted otherwise.
A school bus follows the posted speed limit unless school-district policy determines otherwise.
Driving below a posted minimum is unlawful under normal road, weather and traffic conditions.
Unnecessarily slow driving that blocks normal traffic is unlawful even without a posted minimum.
A slower speed remains permissible when safe operation under the basic speed rule requires it.
Kansas requires passenger-vehicle occupants to use safety restraints.
An officer may stop a vehicle solely for seeing an unbelted adult in a front seat.
An officer may stop a vehicle solely for seeing an unrestrained child in any seating position.
The passenger-car driver must ensure that every child in the car is properly protected by an appropriate restraint.
The cited restraint rule defines a passenger car as a vehicle built for fewer than 10 passengers.
Children younger than 4 must ride in a federally approved child safety seat.
The handbook requires a seat belt for children aged 8 or older.
The handbook identifies the center position in the rear seat as the safest safety-seat location.
Install and use a child safety seat according to its manufacturer's instructions.
Before slowing, turning or changing lanes, check that the movement can be made safely.
Use a signal to tell drivers, cyclists and pedestrians your intended movement.
Give the required signal at least 100 feet before the movement or turn.
Keep a turn signal operating until you are ready to turn.
A vehicle required to have electric turn signals must use them to indicate a turn.
Before turning right from a divided four-lane highway, move into the right lane early.
When turning right from a four-lane divided highway, make a tight turn into the cross street's right lane.
For a left turn on a multilane road, begin in the inside lane near the center line or divider.
When turning left from a multilane road, enter just right of the cross street's center line without swinging wide.
Signs or pavement arrows may authorize turns from multiple lanes.
Do not make a U-turn on a curve or near a hilltop.
A U-turn is prohibited where other drivers cannot see your vehicle from at least 500 feet away.
Follow local ordinances and regulatory signs controlling U-turns.
On a two-way road with two lanes, a left-side pass requires a safe gap and compliance with the speed limit.
Before passing, check ahead for room and behind for another driver beginning to pass.
Use the left-turn signal before beginning a pass on the left.
After passing, signal right before returning to your normal lane.
Return right after a pass only when the entire front of the passed vehicle appears in your inside mirror.
When another vehicle passes you, stay in your lane without accelerating.
Do not pass where a sign forbids it.
The pennant-shaped warning sign marks the start of a no-passing area from the left roadside.
Double solid yellow center lines prohibit traffic from either direction from crossing them.
Finish a pass and return to your lane before an oncoming vehicle is within 200 feet.
The handbook identifies the no-passing warning sign as the only pennant-shaped warning sign.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: A separated multilane highway designated and posted by the transportation secretary may have a 75-mile-per-hour maximum.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: Outside towns, the maximum is 75 miles per hour on a separated multilane highway designated and posted by the Secretary of Transportation, unless a different limit is posted.
changed_existing_facts.issue: Outside-towns scope is omitted, and may have weakens the listed maximum into a possibility.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: Unless posted otherwise, the maximum on a state or federal highway is 65 miles per hour.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: Outside towns, a state or federal highway has a maximum speed of 65 miles per hour unless a different limit is posted.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: Unless posted otherwise, a county or township road has a 55-mile-per-hour maximum.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: Outside towns, a county or township road has a maximum speed of 55 miles per hour unless a different limit is posted.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: The passenger-car driver is responsible for providing appropriate restraints for children riding in the car.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: The passenger-car driver must ensure that every child in the car is properly protected by an appropriate restraint.
changed_existing_facts.issue: Providing a restraint does not preserve the duty to ensure the child is properly protected by it.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: Turn right tightly into the right lane of the street you are entering.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: When turning right from a four-lane divided highway, make a tight turn into the cross street's right lane.
changed_existing_facts.issue: The initiating-road condition is absent from the standalone fact.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: Begin a left turn from the inside lane near the center line or divider.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: For a left turn on a multilane road, begin in the inside lane near the center line or divider.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: Complete a left turn just right of the receiving street's center line without swinging wide.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: When turning left from a multilane road, enter just right of the cross street's center line without swinging wide.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: Use the left signal before starting a pass.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: Use the left-turn signal before beginning a pass on the left.
changed_existing_facts.issue: A pass is broader than the left-side pass described; right-side passing has separate instructions on the same page.

unverifiable_dispositions.original_statement: Do not pass within 100 feet of a bridge, viaduct or tunnel when the view is obstructed.
Do not pass within 100 feet of an intersection.
Do not pass within 100 feet of a railroad grade crossing.
Do not pass in a hill, curve or other designated no-passing area.
Do not pass when the left side ahead lacks a clear view and freedom from oncoming traffic.
A solid yellow center marking on your side prohibits passing.
Do not pass within 100 feet of a roadside emergency vehicle stopped with emergency lights operating.

debts.text: Withheld assertion sec02-F42: Do not pass within 100 feet of a bridge, viaduct or tunnel when the view is obstructed. Reason: Distance and obstruction words match, but the text does not unambiguously attach a passing prohibition to this bullet; do not certify the inferred prohibition. The original meaning, quantity and source page are retained here as unresolved debt; it is not a learner fact.

Withheld assertion sec02-F43: Do not pass within 100 feet of an intersection. Reason: The one-hundred-foot intersection bullet lacks an explicit prohibition in the extracted source; intended rule remains source debt. The original meaning, quantity and source page are retained here as unresolved debt; it is not a learner fact.

Withheld assertion sec02-F44: Do not pass within 100 feet of a railroad grade crossing. Reason: The railroad-crossing distance is present, but the passing prohibition is inferred from a malformed list. The original meaning, quantity and source page are retained here as unresolved debt; it is not a learner fact.

Withheld assertion sec02-F45: Do not pass in a hill, curve or other designated no-passing area. Reason: The intended no-passing scope is not grammatically established, and the authored in a hill is also malformed; issuer text clarification is needed. The original meaning, quantity and source page are retained here as unresolved debt; it is not a learner fact.

Withheld assertion sec02-F46: Do not pass when the left side ahead lacks a clear view and freedom from oncoming traffic. Reason: The inferred prohibition is unconfirmed; lacks a clear view and freedom can also obscure whether either unsafe condition is sufficient. The original meaning, quantity and source page are retained here as unresolved debt; it is not a learner fact.

Withheld assertion sec02-F48: A solid yellow center marking on your side prohibits passing. Reason: The single-solid-line bullet lacks an explicit prohibition; the following double-line sentence does not independently establish the single-line rule. The original meaning, quantity and source page are retained here as unresolved debt; it is not a learner fact.

Withheld assertion sec02-F49: Do not pass within 100 feet of a roadside emergency vehicle stopped with emergency lights operating. Reason: One-hundred-foot distance, stopped vehicle and operating lights are present, but an explicit no-passing instruction is absent from this bullet's lead-in. The original meaning, quantity and source page are retained here as unresolved debt; it is not a learner fact.

The page describes a child-or-booster-seat band from ages four to eight, with a seat-belt exception for height greater than four feet nine inches OR weight greater than eighty pounds; the next bullet requires a belt at eight and older. Retain the strict height and weight inequalities, their OR relationship and the seat-belt outcome while the overlapping age endpoint remains unresolved.
